formex — development status, gaps & the test-data library

Source: DEVELOPMENT-STATUS.md

Status snapshot, 2026-10-25. A companion to the user-facing Type Atlas vignette (vignettes/formex-type-atlas.Rmd). The Atlas describes what each type is; this note records what is built, what is not, and what the detectors were tested against. Numbers are from the shipped ontology (fx_ontology(), 96 variants) and the dev test library (dev/feature_matrix_all.rds, 4,036 columns). The dev/ tree is local scaffolding and is not shipped or version-controlled, so the library figures are a point-in-time measurement, not a build artifact.

1. Where the engine stands

The two public verbs are both wired and pass the suite (121 tests, 0 failures):

  • guess_data_type() — two-stage router → verifier, returning the $route record plus the legacy fields.
  • fx_stabilize() — the transform executor (fx_transform() + a verb library) that the original integration plan listed as the critical missing path. It is now built; the DSL parser and ~31 verbs run against the ontology recipes.

Still per the plan and not formex’s to build: the datagoodr governance-file schema and the actual extraction of the moved files out of datagoodr (see INTEGRATION-NOTES.md).

2. Implementation coverage (what has a working detector)

Of 97 ontology variants, 48 (49%) are marked implemented = "yes" — a wired, exercised detector. The rest are declared recipes (data_format / transform / stable_format / import_rule are populated) waiting on a detector, verb, or gazetteer.

v7 session update. Coverage rose 36 → 46 by wiring test-backed, foil-selective detectors (data-raw/wire_detectors_v7.R): day_of_week / month_of_year (new as_dow / as_moy), first_name, quarter, domain, usd (new is_currency_amount — symbol-required), place (lookup:place), min_max range, and point / polygon (is_wkt_geometry, keyword-gated). Key finding worth carrying forward: a selective recipe is necessary but not sufficient to route — the learned router never shortlists very rare mask leaves (array, version, reporting_period confirm in isolation but never reach the verifier), so they stay unimplemented until either the router has training cases or they join the verifier’s always-on set (as the geometry family now does). Two verb bugs were fixed along the way: the DSL arg parser left a trailing ] on verb[arg], and as_range was loose enough to claim nested arrays as ranges.

Later in the session: the disambiguator landed (a disambiguator / collision_group column + a cardinality tie-break wired into the verifier, resolving the geographic grouping-vs-key and the cross-type place↔︎geographic collisions; fx_validate_ontology() fails on an undeclared collision). fx_stabilize() gained a conversion_log and a warning when present values are dropped to NA, so silent data loss is surfaced. From datagoodr’s dplyr::starwars report: a named-color leaf (text/color/color_name + is_color_name()) fixes color words leaking to geographic, and a write_numeric edge lets plain measurements stabilize to numeric; and a tags detector (is_tags) wires categorical/multiselect/tags for delimited list columns. Coverage is now 48/97; 92 detectors; 121 tests.

3. Unimplemented detectors, grouped

Highest leverage first (the mechanism tells you whether the work is a detector, a verb, or a reference list).

number — the biggest gap (0 of 23). Every quantity, portion, currency, range and coordinate variant is unimplemented. - shape (not subtype-detectable from values; need the header): measurement, count, rate, ratio, duration, score, index, rank, probability, odds, percent, percentile. - mask (detector + verb is real work): currency/{balance,usd,euro}, range/{comma_pair,to_range,confidence_interval}, coordinate/{lat_lon dms, lat_lon iso6709, lon_lat, lat, lon}.

boolean (0 of 5). is_boolean() exists and recognizes the two-state vocabulary, but no binary variant is marked implemented and the class (indicator / presence / status / response / mixed) needs the header. Worth reconciling: the detector is shipped but the ontology rows say otherwise.

structured (0 of 6). Detectors exist (is_json, is_wkt_geometry, is_geojson, is_wkb) but collection/{list,array}, record/{object, key_value} and geometry/{point,polygon} are not wired; recipes pass through as literal text.

temporal (6 of 12). Open: period/{quarter, reporting_period}, phase/{hour_of_day, day_of_week, month_of_year, week_of_year}.

text (14 of 24). Open: name/{first_name, last_name, full_name, place, handle} (lexicon-bound), text/{label, title, long, serialized} (none), web/domain.

categorical (7 of 13). Open: scale/{likert, rating, ranking, grade_level}, multiselect/tags, mutually_exclusive/missingness_reason — all none, i.e. codebook-gated.

identifier (9 of 10). Only id/version remains.

4. Repo hygiene gaps

  • Ontology drift. Resolved: the stale data-types/…_v6.csv duplicate was removed; fx_ontology() reads inst/extdata/ (the authority). (Older design snapshots …_v2/v3/v4.csv remain for history.)
  • No CI. Resolved: a standard r-lib R-CMD-check workflow (.github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml) builds the package, runs the suite, and builds the vignettes on push / PR to main.
  • Version is still 0.0.0.9000; nothing published.
  • The benign NAs introduced by coercion to integer range warning fires ~18× across the suite (numeric-coercion paths) — cosmetic, worth bounding.

5. The test-data library

The detectors are measured against a unified library of 4,036 real and synthetic columns, one row per column, assembled from three sources and crosswalked to the formex ontology.

5.1 Columns ingested, by source

source columns nature
Sherlock / VizNet 3,423 real columns sampled from the ~137K-column VizNet test split; 78-type Sherlock label vocabulary. Labels derive from headers, so they are noisier — deliberately, as hard negatives
synthetic_temporal 436 generated columns across the temporal leaves, exact ground truth, an easy + mutated-hard mix, to give the router the dense, balanced temporal neighbourhood the wild corpora lack
GitTables 177 real columns with independent headers (so usable for the name-side evaluation too)
total 4,036

By formex data type the library leans heavily text/categorical/number:

text 1339 · categorical 1283 · number 667 · temporal 553 · identifier 149 · unknown 38 · structured 5 · boolean 2

5.2 How they were standardized into one library

A corpus-agnostic banking core (dev/bank_core.R) turns every source into the same shape, so everything downstream is identical regardless of origin:

  1. Record. Each source column becomes a record list(values, label, table_id, header) via a per-corpus adapter (GitTables CSV, Sherlock parquet, the temporal generator). Heterogeneous value encodings — stringified Python lists, Arrow list-columns, materialized vectors — are parsed to a clean character vector; headers are snake-cased.
  2. Crosswalk / resolve. A resolver maps the source’s own label vocabulary to a formex ontology coordinate through a *-crosswalk-v4.csv whose v4_type / v4_class / v4_subclass columns are the v6 path, emitting a semantic_type_id + variant_id against the live ontology.
  3. Triage & bank. fx_triage_field() → fx_make_test_case() writes a uniform schema-v2 JSON test case per column, with an exclusion log for rejects.
  4. Diversity sampling (Sherlock). 137K columns is too many and mostly redundant, so cases are chosen by farthest-point selection over fx_type_signature() distance (capped per type) rather than a random draw — maximizing shape diversity and surfacing hard negatives.
  5. Feature matrix. dev/build_feature_matrix.R assembles the labeled substrate the router/verifier train on: one row per banked column, the value-only v2 feature profile (~471 features) plus public-domain gazetteer membership features, joined to the label axes (data_type → variant_id). Result: feature_matrix_all.rds, 4,036 × 491.

5.3 Test cases per formex variant (after crosswalk)

Crosswalking to the ontology, 53 of 96 variants carry at least one test case; 43 carry none. Among variants that have cases: median 24, mean 73, max 611. The distribution is very uneven:

cases per variant 1 2–5 6–10 11–25 26–50 51–100 100+
variants 6 9 4 11 5 6 12

Best-covered variants:

variant cases path
n0044-f01 611 categorical / unordered
n0046-f01 459 categorical / iso_country
n0028-f01 371 text / organization
n0027-f01 359 text / first_name
n0001-f01 223 number / measurement
n0059-f01 182 temporal / calendar
n0002-f01 148 number / count
n0073-f01 77 identifier / ein

The coverage and the implementation status do not line up, which is the main testing gap:

  • 18 implemented variants have zero test cases — detectors with no independent column in the library to confirm them against.
  • 35 variants have test cases but are not implemented — labeled data waiting for a detector/verb (much of it the number/quantity and shape block, which the crosswalk can label but the engine cannot yet type by value).
  • Whole families are thin or empty: number/coordinate (3 cases), structured/geometry (1), boolean/binary (2), text/contact (2). Any accuracy claim there rests on a handful of columns.

5.4 Caveats

  • The library is banked against an earlier ontology snapshot (the build scripts reference a 92–94-row ontology); the crosswalk targets v6 paths, so labels resolve, but the 96-row shipped ontology has moved since.
  • dev/stabilize_rate.R — the source of the per-mechanism confirm rates — reads only the Sherlock + synthetic-temporal banks (feature_matrix.rds, 3,859 columns), not GitTables, and counts none / open-set types as not-stabilized.
  • Sherlock labels come from headers, so a slice of the “truth” is itself noisy; this is intentional (hard negatives) but caps the achievable top-1.

6. Benchmark-driven detector priorities (2026-10-29)

The benchmark is still in development — not yet frozen for published reference. The frozen set now covers all 97 ontology variants (was 51): data-raw/scaffold_gap_cases.R banks one format-faithful case per previously-uncovered variant into dev/bank_v2 (values from the data-raw/datatypes/*.R detector fixtures, or a seeded generator where no fixture exists), and build_benchmark.R now bundles the full set in inst/extdata/benchmark_full.rds. These scaffolds are method = "scaffold_synthetic", confidence = "low" — regression anchors and a gap probe, not gold-vetted corpus columns; confirm/relabel before any published accuracy claim.

Running fx_benchmark() over the newly-covered variants splits cleanly into two very different kinds of failure. The split, not the headline number, is the finding — it says whether the work is router tuning or new detector code.

6.1 P0 — router recall: 11 implemented detectors are dark

These variants are implemented = "yes" with a selective recipe, yet the router never routes to them (prediction is <none> or a wrong neighbour). No new detector code is needed — the fix is in the shortlist/router. This is the single highest-ROI item and confirms the §2 note that a selective recipe is necessary but not sufficient to route; the learned router never shortlists very rare mask leaves.

variant path predicted instead
n0040-f01 text/color/hex <none>
n0041-f01 text/color/rgb measurement
n0042-f01 text/color/hsl measurement
n0043-f01 text/color/cmyk <none>
n0036-f01 text/web/ip <none>
n0037-f01 text/web/mac <none>
n0039-f01 text/contact/phone <none>
n0032-f01 text/postal/po_box unordered
n0064-f01 temporal/period/month calendar
n0022-f01 text/text/literal <none>
n0073-f05 identifier/id/administrative (issn) date_range

Action. Add confirmable mask leaves to the verifier’s always-on set (as the geometry family already is) or seed the learned router with these cases so it shortlists them. issn → date_range is a genuine confusability bug (NNNN-NNNN collides with a date range) — give it a hard_negative / disambiguator entry.

✅ LANDED (2026-10-29). All eleven now route. The fix was the always-on verifier set, not a retrain: the dark mask leaves (hex, rgb, hsl, cmyk, ip, mac, phone, month, issn) plus the whole boolean family are forced into the candidate set in .fx_route_verify(), and each was given a SELECTIVE recipe that reuses its existing detector (as_rgb/as_hsl/as_cmyk/ as_ip/as_mac/as_po_box/as_month, as_hex/as_phone/as_issn tightened), so the foil gate still blocks a false leaf. po_box (already mask+lexicon, so already always-on) only needed its recipe. The issn ↔︎ date_range collision is resolved in the recipe, not by cardinality (benchmark ISSN columns repeat, so a cardinality rule would pick the wrong leaf): as_range yields a checksum-valid NNNN-NNNN to the issn leaf, exactly as it yields a YYYY-MM to month — but it keeps a plausible year-year span (both 19xx/20xx) as a range, so 2000-2005 stays date_range. month vs calendar is broken by a month-granularity tie-break (year+month, no day). Per-type type-accuracy before → after on the full set:

leaf before after leaf before after
hex 0.00 0.80 po_box 0.00 1.00
rgb 0.00 1.00 month 0.00 0.80
hsl 0.00 1.00 literal 0.00 0.50
cmyk 0.00 1.00 issn 0.25 0.50
ip 0.00 0.75 phone 0.00 0.67
mac 0.00 1.00

The sub-1.0 cases are synthetic-slice artifacts, not misroutes: the bare-hex a1b2c3 slice is intentionally rejected (it collides with short hashes/ids), the IPv6 :: degenerate form, the NNNN-NNNX ISSN slice carries invalid synthetic checksums, and literal fires only on a recognizable typed MIXTURE (2 of its 4 deliberately-mixed slices qualify; the others are too sparse to call). The literal passthrough is gated last and narrow, so it never steals a clean type or an unknown/heterogeneous junk column.

6.2 P0 — the boolean data type is 0%

presence / status / response / mixed all misroute (to unordered or <none>); acc_data_type for boolean is 0.00 on the benchmark. is_boolean() exists but no binary variant is wired, so an entire data type is invisible. Wire the boolean verifier into the always-on set and reconcile the ontology implemented flags.

✅ LANDED (2026-10-29). boolean is detected at the data_type level across every binary vocabulary. as_boolean was broadened past yes/no/t/f/1/0/on/off to the two-state status/presence vocabularies (active/inactive, enabled/disabled, open/closed, present/absent, x), and all five binary variants are forced into the always-on set. A third state NAs out and drops confirm below threshold, so a genuine multi-state categorical is not captured. acc_data_type for boolean goes 0.00 → ~1.00 (every subtype now resolves data_type == "boolean"); the specific subtype stays coarse (it is header-dependent — the verifier predicts indicator for all of them, so acc_type for the family is ~0.10, which is expected and documented). The stale implemented flags were reconciled: boolean binary (n0054..n0058) and person last_name/full_name (n0027-f02/f03, which the benchmark already hits) are now yes.

Headline movement (full set, 917 cases). data_type 0.799 → 0.855, family 0.737 → 0.797, semantic_type 0.692 → 0.735, headline 0.744 → 0.798; text 0.496 → 0.723 and identifier 0.426 → 0.447 by data_type, with no per-variant regression (fx_coverage_gaps() clean; date_range, calendar, clean numerics/zips all held). The learned router was not retrained — the scaffold cases are confidence=low measurement anchors.

6.3 P1 — number masks (real detector + verb work)

implemented = "no", mask-detectable from values, so each needs a detector and a stabilize verb: balance, euro (currency), min_max, confidence_interval (range), lat, lat_lon, lon_lat (coordinate). They misroute to measurement / min_max / rank. Highest value in the number block because the surface form is typable (unlike the shape subtypes below).

✅ LANDED — currency (euro) + coordinates (2026-10-29). euro (n0011-f01) and the coordinate PAIR leaves lat_lon (n0018-f01 DMS/decimal, n0018-f02 ISO 6709) and lon_lat (n0019-f01 DMS/decimal) now route at type-accuracy 1.00 on the benchmark, with no per-variant regression (headline 0.800 → 0.804 on the full set). euro reuses the symbol-parameterized .fx_currency_amount() (the generic mechanism behind as_usd/as_euro; adding a currency is now a one-liner). The coordinate family is new (R/dt-coordinate.R: is_coord_latlon / is_coord_lonlat / is_iso6709 + as_coord_* verbs), canonicalizing DMS / decimal / ISO 6709 pairs to lat-first decimal degrees. All four joined the always-on verifier set (they route without a retrain) and ship banked format slices. One supporting fix: as_range now rejects a descending comma/to pair (34.1, -118.1, lat > lon) — a valid range is ascending — so a western/southern-hemisphere decimal coordinate falls through to the coordinate leaf instead of being claimed as a min_max range; ascending ranges (1.2, 3.4) are unchanged.

Deferred (header-gated, Phase C — not value-typable): balance (n0009-f01, a symbol-less bare number) and the bare lat / lon singletons (n0020/n0021, a lone decimal in range). A value-only detector for these would manufacture false leaves; they belong to the name-side/arbiter work (§7.4). min_max to_range / confidence_interval remain for a later pass.

6.4 P2 — shape numerics and codebook-gated types (fail safe or need header)

  • number/shape: probability, odds, percentile land graceful (correct data_type, no committed subtype) — they fail safely and are low urgency; rate misroutes to measurement. None are subtype-typable from values alone.
  • categorical/none: likert, missingness_reason and text/text/serialized need a codebook/header; low yield from values.
  • temporal/phase: hour_of_day, week_of_year are bare small integers, genuinely ambiguous with number without a header.
  • structured non-geometry: array, object, key_value route to <none> / tags; is_json / is_wkb exist but are not wired for these. (point / polygon already hit — now regression-covered.)

6.5 Already correct (now regression-anchored)

Nine previously-untested variants hit on the first benchmark and now have a guard: geographic (×3), administrative isbn/doi/orcid (×3), point, polygon, color_name.

Housekeeping. ✅ Done — the stale implemented flags for person (n0027-f02/f03) and the boolean binary variants were flipped to yes in the §6.1/§6.2 pass.

Reproduce: Rscript data-raw/scaffold_gap_cases.R && Rscript data-raw/build_benchmark.R, then fx_benchmark(fx_benchmark_data("full")) and fx_coverage_gaps().

6.6 Format-sliced depth for the P0 types (2026-10-29)

The gap scaffold gave each P0 variant exactly one canonical case (n=1, synthetic, confidence=low) — enough to measure coverage but not format drift, the real failure surface. data-raw/scaffold_format_slices.R now banks several cases per P0 variant, one per distinct surface shape (positive, single-shape columns of ~34 rows; values sliced from the data-raw/datatypes/*.R fixtures by regex, or seeded-generated where the fixtures lack a shape). This adds 50 cases across the 15 P0 variants (full set 867 → 917; every P0 variant now carries 3–6 cases), labelled method="scaffold_format_slice", corpus="scaffold_fmt", confidence="low", with the exact shape recorded in label.format_label / original_label / notes. Shapes added:

  • hex #RRGGBB, #RGB, bare RRGGBB, 0xRRGGBB
  • rgb r,g,b, spaced r, g, b, functional rgb(r,g,b)
  • hsl h, s%, l%, functional hsl(…); cmyk fractional c,m,y,k, functional cmyk(…)
  • ip IPv4 dotted, IPv6 full, IPv6 compressed (::)
  • mac colon, hyphen, Cisco-dotted; phone NANP dashed / parens / dotted, E.164 +1-…, international +CC …
  • po_box PO BOX n / P.O. Box n / POB n / Box n
  • month yyyymm / Mon YYYY / YYYY-MM / full name
  • literal 3 deliberately heterogeneous mixed-content columns
  • issn NNNN-NNNN / check-digit NNNN-NNNX / ISSN-prefixed
  • boolean presence (x·blank / 1·blank / present·absent), status (active·inactive / enabled·disabled / on·off / open·closed), response (yes·no / Y·N / true·false / T·F / 1·0), mixed (2 multi-encoding columns)

Per-format finding: the P0 failures are systemic, not shape-specific. The router misroutes on every shape of nearly every P0 variant — it never reaches these leaves at all, so format drift is not yet the differentiator (it will become one once §6.1/§6.2 land the routing). Two exceptions are the actionable signal:

  • hex #RRGGBB lands graceful (recognized as text, subtype dropped), while its drift variants (#RGB, bare RRGGBB, 0xRRGGBB) all misroute — the canonical hash-6 form is the only shape the pipeline half-recognizes.
  • issn hits only when the literal ISSN prefix is present; bare NNNN-NNNN misroutes (the date_range collision from §6.1) and the check-digit NNNN-NNNX form lands graceful. The prefix token is the disambiguator — direct evidence for the §6.1 hard_negative/disambiguator action.
  • boolean is 0% across all 20 cases (every shape, every subtype), re-confirming §6.2.

✅ Post-fix per-format split (§6.1/§6.2 landed). The format slices did exactly their job as regression anchors. Hit rate on the scaffold_fmt slices after the fix: rgb/hsl/cmyk/mac/po_box 1.00, phone 0.80, month/hex 0.75, ip 0.67, issn/literal 0.33. The residual misses are shape-specific and expected, not routing gaps: bare-RRGGBB hex (collides with short hashes, left out on purpose), IPv6 ::, the invalid-checksum NNNN-NNNX ISSN slice, and the sparser literal mixes. Boolean is 0% at the subtype level by design (the subtype is header-dependent) but ~100% at the data_type level — the must-fix.

These cases are regression anchors for the P0 work: when a routing fix lands, the per-format hit/graceful/misroute split (group fx_benchmark() output by format_label) shows which shapes it recovered, not just a single number. This is recommendation #1 of the benchmark review (format depth); the hard-negative/confusability bank is a separate follow-up.

Reproduce: Rscript data-raw/scaffold_format_slices.R && Rscript data-raw/build_benchmark.R, then fx_benchmark(fx_benchmark_data("full")) and join format_label back by case_id for the per-shape split.

7. Forward plan (2026-10-29 addendum)

A roadmap for the two open fronts — finishing the detector set and improving the router — plus four design decisions that came out of looking hard at the shipped model (inst/extdata/router_xgb.rds, 3,853 cases × 441 features, 47 classes, OOF top-1 0.771 / top-5 0.946 / top-8 0.965).

7.1 Detector implementation roadmap

The remaining unimplemented variants split by mechanism, and the mechanism dictates the work. Sequenced by leverage:

Phase A — mask detectors (value-detectable, highest routable payoff). These are real detector+verb work but the values carry the signal, so they both confirm and can be learned-routed once cases exist. - number/currency/{balance,usd,euro} — ✅ done (usd, euro). usd and euro share the symbol-parameterized .fx_currency_amount() mask (unit_type USD/EUR); adding a currency is a one-liner. balance stays deferred — it is symbol-less, so header-gated (Phase C), not a value mask. write_* currency renderer / cross-currency conversion is still open (§7.1 renderers). - number/range/{comma_pair,to_range,confidence_interval} — min_max done; add the CI form and the lo to hi style. (as_range now also rejects a descending comma pair, reserving those for the coordinate leaf — see §6.3.) - number/coordinate/{lat_lon dms/decimal, iso6709, lon_lat dms/decimal} — ✅ done. New R/dt-coordinate.R detectors + as_coord_* decimal-degree canonicalizer, all at type-accuracy 1.00 (§6.3). The bare lat / lon singletons stay deferred (header-gated: a lone in-range decimal is not value-typable). - structured/geometry/{point,polygon} and structured/collection|record — the detectors already exist (is_wkt_geometry, is_geojson, is_wkb, is_json); the work is wiring the ontology rows implemented = yes and giving them a pass-through/parse recipe. Geometry is already in the verifier’s always-on set, so it routes without the model (see §7.6). - boolean/binary reconciliation (quick win). is_boolean() is shipped and works; the rows say unimplemented. Wire + mark; the class (indicator/presence/status/response) is header-gated and belongs in Phase C.

Carry-forward rule from the v7 session: a selective recipe is necessary but not sufficient to route. A new mask leaf that confirms in isolation (array, version, reporting_period) is still invisible to the learned router until it has training cases or joins the always-on set. Every Phase-A detector ships with banked cases, or it does not count as routable (§7.6).

Phase B — lexicon detectors (need a reference list). text/name/{last_name, full_name, place, handle}. first_name and place landed; last_name/full_name reuse the surname gazetteer, handle needs a small pattern+lexicon. Gated only by shippable, licence-clean lists.

Phase C — shape / none types are NOT a detector problem. The whole number/quantity block (measurement, count, rate, ratio, duration, score, index, rank, probability, percent, percentile), the boolean/categorical classes, and text/{label,title,long} are not value-typable by subtype — a column of doubles cannot tell you it is a rate rather than a ratio. These need the column header/codebook, i.e. the name-side (nm_*) feature path, which is currently dark (§7.4). Phase C is therefore a router/arbiter task (turn the name features on and fuse them), not a detector task. Do not ship value-only detectors for these; they will only manufacture false leaves.

7.2 Router improvement plan

  1. Parity guard. ✅ Landed 2026-10-29. The artifact stamps extractor_version = 2.0 but nothing asserted the live fx_extract_features still matched it. .fx_router_artifact() now checks at load time: if FEATURE_EXTRACTOR_VERSION != art$extractor_version (or the artifact is unstamped), it drops the learned router and falls back to signature with a one-time warning. This was the one failure mode that silently returned garbage (the original “scored at chance” bug).
  2. Un-blind the dropped feature classes (§7.4). Bank cases — synthetic where the type is rare-but-regular (the bank_temporal recipe) — for the types the corpus currently has zero examples of: SSN, EIN, UUID, IPv4, ZIP+4, YYYYMM, hex hashes, JSON, DMS coordinates, international phone, scientific notation. This simultaneously (a) adds the classes the model can predict and
    1. gives the rx_* features variance so they stop being dropped.
  3. Name-side fusion (unlocks Phase C). Bank columns with headers, feed the name to the extractor so the 17 nm_* features compute, and train either a name-aware model or a late-fusion arbiter (value-router ⊕ name-signal). This is the only route to the header-gated types.
  4. Rebalance. The corpus leans text/categorical/number; top-1 by match_kind already shows mask (0.964) trailing genome/lexicon (~1.0). Stratify or class-weight so thin types are not drowned.
  5. Calibrate the depth gates. The learned router’s top-1 probability sets truncation depth directly (≥0.50 → 3, ≥0.25 → 1). Plot a reliability curve and set those cut-points from calibration rather than by hand.
  6. CI + non-regression gate. Wire fx_benchmark() + fx_benchmark_compare() into the retrain step; a new artifact ships only if it does not regress the shipped one on any level or the per-match_kind top-k recall.

7.3 Should we sunset the legacy flat detector path?

Verdict: deprecate, don’t delete — and demote it now. It is not synergistic with the router path; it is a parallel, older contract.

Reasons it still earns its place today: - Backward contract. $guess / $ontology / $candidates and the flat coordinate axes (data_type / data_subtype / data_class / data_format) are consumed by guess_column() and five test suites; the flat data_format axis is not 1:1 with the v6/v7 format_style/unit_type axes. - Independent fallback. It needs neither xgboost nor the ontology CSV — pure predicate scoring. When .fx_route_verify() errors (it is wrapped in tryCatch → NULL), the legacy fields still answer. - The detectors are shared, not duplicated. The is_* predicates are reused by the verifier (recipe = detector + transform), so keeping the detectors costs nothing; only the flat scoring + flat ontology crosswalk is redundant.

Reasons to retire it on a schedule: - Two ontologies to maintain. R/00-data-type-ontology.R is a hand-kept flat crosswalk that can drift from the v6/v7 ontology — a standing correctness risk. - Cost. score_data_type() runs all 88 detectors on every call — exactly the O(all-detectors) scan the router was built to avoid — yet it runs unconditionally because route = TRUE is the default.

Plan: (1) ✅ Landed 2026-10-29 — guess_data_type(..., legacy = FALSE) skips the flat scan and returns only the $route record (legacy fields present but empty); measured at ~13% of the full per-call runtime on a typical column, since it no longer scores all 88 detectors. (2) document $guess/$ontology as deprecated-but-supported; (3) remove only after datagoodr and any flat-axis consumers migrate to $route, and after v7’s format_style/unit_type fully subsume the flat data_format axis. Target: drop in the release that removes format_label, alongside the router retrain that release already forces (§7.6).

7.4 Feature hygiene: why 36 of 477 features drop out

Measured by reproducing train_router.R’s variance filter over the 3,859 training columns (data-raw/ diagnostic). The features are not defective — the drop is corpus-driven, and it splits three ways:

bucket n examples reading
all-NA (never computes) 17 nm_amt, nm_date, nm_person, nm_id, … (16 nm_*) + chk_ein_prefix_rate the name-side block is gated off — training is value-only, no header is fed, so these are structurally absent, not broken. They light up the moment §7.2(3) feeds headers.
constant everywhere (sd 0) 18 rx_ssn, rx_ein, rx_uuid, rx_ipv4, rx_zip9, rx_yyyymm, rx_hexhash, rx_jsonfrag, rx_latlon_dms, rx_phone_intl, rx_sci_not; in_is_numeric/date/factor/logical, is_constant, pct_missing split in two (below)
constant where present (gated, sd 0) 1 range_epoch_ms (computes on 18.8% of cols, all 0) near-degenerate on this corpus

So the answer to “universal or selective?” is both, and the distinction is the useful part:

  • The in_is_* flags, is_constant, and pct_missing are structurally constant in the banked pipeline: recon() always yields a character vector with no NAs and >1 value, so input-class / missingness / degeneracy flags can never vary. These are genuinely uninformative here (they would vary on raw typed input) — harmless to drop.
  • The rx_* regex-hit rates are constant at exactly 0 — confirmed over the full 4,036-column matrix, zero non-zero columns. They are not broken; the corpus simply contains no SSN / EIN / UUID / IPv4 / ZIP+4 / YYYYMM / hex-hash / JSON / DMS-coordinate / intl-phone / scientific-notation columns. A rate that is 0 for every training column carries no signal and is dropped.

The payoff: the dropped-rx_* set is a free blind-spot diagnostic. It enumerates, independently of the label crosswalk, exactly the types the learned router has no training signal for — and it corroborates §5.3’s “18 implemented variants have zero test cases.” These are the same types §7.2(2) targets, and they map straight onto the number / structured / thin-identifier gaps in §3. Recommendation: add an assertion to the retrain script that any rx_* feature dropped for zero variance names the type to bank next, so the gap is surfaced at train time rather than discovered by inspection.

7.5 Flagging underperforming detectors (difficulty-aware)

Shipped. fx_coverage_gaps() formerly used a flat gate (max_accuracy = 0.5, min_support = 3). The objection was correct: a universal threshold conflates three different things — intrinsic difficulty, thin/noisy support, and a genuine detector bug. The flat gate is replaced with four signals and two action buckets, so each flag points at a fix:

  1. Per-match_kind target, not a single number. Achievable precision is a function of mechanism: genome/lexicon/mask+lexicon types can reach ~0.95; shape/none types are header-gated and should be excluded from value accuracy entirely, not scored at 0. Set the target by match_kind.
  2. Baseline-relative, not absolute. Flag a type where the learned router underperforms the signature router (run both via router=). A type hard for everyone is difficulty, not a bug; a type where learned < model-free floor is a real regression. (fx_benchmark_compare() already computes these deltas.)
  3. Stress-delta (robustness). Use fx_stress_grid(): flag types whose accuracy collapses under mild perturbation (low whitespace / case / contamination) relative to their own clean-tier score. Brittleness to a space or a stray uppercase is a detector bug regardless of absolute accuracy, and fx_contamination_curve() already measures the shape.
  4. Support-aware confidence. Put a Wilson interval on the accuracy estimate; only flag “low-accuracy” when the interval’s upper bound is below target, so thin-support types are not flagged on noise.

Two buckets, two fixes: needs-cases (thin support, or absent from the corpus → bank/generate data, §7.2(2)) vs needs-detector-work (adequate support but accuracy upper-bounded below target, losing to the signature baseline, or stress-brittle → fix the predicate/recipe); header-gated shape/none types with adequate support are excluded, the rest ok. fx_coverage_gaps() gained a target argument (default by match_kind via .FX_COVERAGE_TARGETS), optional baseline= and stress= run arguments, wilson_upper / baseline_delta / stress_drop columns, and emits a bucket label in place of the old "ok" / "low-accuracy" / "low-support" flag. With include_absent = TRUE (the default) it also walks the full ontology and emits a support == 0 needs-cases row for every live variant that never appears in the corpus — the blind spots the per-case signals cannot see.

Not yet wired: tying the dropped-rx_* feature set into needs-cases. That set is enumerated at retrain time (§7.4), not persisted as a loadable object, so there is no programmatic handle for fx_coverage_gaps() to read yet; wiring it in waits on the retrain script banking the dropped-rx_* names as an artifact.

7.6 Router refresh: cadence & triggers

The learned router predicts over a fixed 47-class set (art$levels). Inference maps predicted ids to ontology rows by match(), so the framework degrades gracefully, it does not break: an ontology id not in art$levels is simply never shortlisted; an art$levels id no longer in the ontology is dropped. The question is therefore not “does X break the router” but “does X leave the router blind to something it should route.”

MUST retrain (correctness): - Any fx_extract_features change — a feature added, removed, reordered, or recomputed. The artifact bakes in feature names, column order, and median imputations; a mismatch is silent train/serve skew. Bump FEATURE_EXTRACTOR_VERSION, retrain, and rely on the §7.2(1) parity guard in the interim. - Removal of format_label in v7 (the router trains on it; already the deferred retrain in ONTOLOGY-V7-PLAN.md §5).

SHOULD retrain (coverage): - A new routable semantic_type_id added to the ontology — to add it as a predictable class. (Interim: add high-precision types to the verifier’s always-on set, as geometry/email/color-name already are — this makes them routable with no retrain.) - New or expanded training cases for an under-covered type, especially the §7.4 zero-example types — to lift its top-k recall. - A benchmark regression where fx_benchmark_compare() shows learned losing to signature on a level or match_kind.

NO retrain needed: - A new detector/recipe for an existing class — the verifier picks it up and the router already shortlists the class. - Deprecating a row (ids are never renumbered/reused; match() handles it). - Pure fx_stabilize verb/transform additions (they are not router inputs).

Cadence: there is no fixed schedule, nor should there be — retrain is event-driven by the triggers above, gated by the §7.2(6) non-regression check. The one standing recommendation is the parity guard, so that the “correctness” triggers can never fail silently between retrains.
